title: Drainage bags and joint shipping for customers holding two Urology and Continence Supply Programs
content:
When a customer holds two Urology and Continence Supply Programs, each program keeps its own allowance. Two items are treated differently: drainage bags, and the timing of refills that fall due close together.

## Drainage bags once per customer

Drainage bags (A4357 and A4358) are allowed once per customer. They ship only on the program that is not closed, has the earlier enrolled date, and has a product line that lists them. The other program receives none. The test reads the customer's programs, with their enrolled dates, statuses and product lines.

*Hypothetical:* an external catheter program enrolled in January and an indwelling catheter program enrolled in May, both open. Both product lines list drainage bags, so bags ship only on the January program. If the January program closes, the May program becomes the program with the earlier enrolled date that is not closed.

## Joint shipping

When the earliest permitted ship dates of the two programs fall within the tier's consolidation span in calendar days of each other, both refills ship together on the later of the two dates.

*Hypothetical (10-day span):* earliest dates of the 3rd and the 11th are 8 days apart, so both ship on the 11th. Earliest dates of the 3rd and the 20th are 17 days apart, so each ships on its own date.
